summary: The current candidate remains compatible with all 21 unchanged criteria. It preserves current summary/query/header behavior, replaces a diagnostic sequence without dropping its outcomes, and bounds owned-record observations without claiming unrelated account preservation. No concrete mandatory compatibility defect was found. Native G1-G4 and final release proof remain required.

compatibility_assessments.assessment: The changed runtime-adapter edition is used rather than restored to the superseded blanket preservation instruction. Header hashing is explicitly first-record identity, not whole-log integrity. Reader/incarnation-bound handles and stat-bound signed continuation preserve access scope. Raw logs, complete role/problem inputs, native pages, actual cells and callbacks remain required. Rebinding the proof import closure to the reader/header/policy/Broker changes is explicit.

The candidate includes actual generic worker implementation/testing and independent manager verification; complete handoff; typed supervision and same-ID resume; helper reset and peer recheck; independent real native memory/ontology publication with negative cases; and complete release/stop observations. The separate Director-default case is expressly required in the prepared packet. The 18-start/120-cell figures remain design targets subject to exact measured sequence preparation, not authorization or provider caps. G1 cannot pass G2-G4.

Explicit owned-records-v1 selection preserves strict existing modes. It binds actual owned IDs and returned paths, original device/inode/type/link/header, owned index keys/fields in a consistent snapshot, fixed canaries, actor epochs and caller/grant/owner provenance. Startup writer closure and bounded effects must be established before baseline, then rechecked at transitions and closure. Unrelated rows remain unobserved and no whole-account equality claim is permitted. Missing scope/dependency evidence holds execution; there is no automatic ambient allowance, global-idle assumption, privacy exception or silent fallback. These required gates are coherent design conditions, not newly observed enforcement.

criteria.criterion: Neutral starter has no live identity/branch set, standing grant, schedule or autonomous-write permission.
criteria.assessment: Retained neutral starter and absent operational entitlements are unchanged.

criteria.criterion: Missing, malformed, expired or incompatible selections produce precise unavailable/blocked diagnostics.
criteria.assessment: Existing precise blocked/unavailable diagnostics remain; missing owned-record identity, writer closure or dependencies holds the new mode.

criteria.criterion: Project specialization is capability-only; standing entitlements remain absent until deliberately accepted at adoption.
criteria.assessment: Capability-only specialization and deliberate entitlement acceptance remain unchanged.

criteria.criterion: AGENTS.md, README sections, generated wiki and Task responses have distinct owners and update routes.
criteria.assessment: Distinct AGENTS, descriptive README, generated wiki and Task-history owner routes are retained.

criteria.criterion: Overrides, generators, stable identities and protected sections resolve conservatively; unknown/mixed targets hold unsafe edits.
criteria.assessment: Protected classification, source/section identity, generators and conservative unknown/mixed handling are retained.

criteria.criterion: Grants bind actor/project/branch/policy/source/payload/scope/owner and freshness; valid standing entitlements avoid redundant approval.
criteria.assessment: Exact grant bindings and standing-entitlement behavior remain; compact turns do not remove actual owner preconditions.

criteria.criterion: Candidate-controlled code and environment cannot alter broker policy, credentials or effective approval logic.
criteria.assessment: New reader/header/policy/Broker imports must join the verified trusted closure; native filesystem/tool/network enforcement remains mandatory.

criteria.criterion: Broker routes canonical mutations to their existing helper owners and rejects arbitrary shell instructions.
criteria.assessment: G1 performs real typed Broker requests and canonical owner mutations, with no driver-private result injection or arbitrary shell route.

criteria.criterion: Caller identity comes from the trusted native request envelope and current manager binding, not an actor string in model arguments; workers cannot read private grants or broker credentials.
criteria.assessment: Reader/incarnation-bound handles and actual callbacks preserve caller identity; separate native manager/owner grant checks and worker denials remain.

criteria.criterion: One controller/charter is selected per execution; reading a charter does not activate it.
criteria.assessment: The candidate retains Director default, inert charter presence and a separate Director observation before claiming full NP-002.

criteria.criterion: Specialist responsibilities, qualifications, role reads, scope and stopping rules are explicit; generic Director use and category rules are preserved.
criteria.assessment: G1 uses one generic worker with corrections returned to it; complete complex and extra-complex teams remain required in G2.

criteria.criterion: New provenance is schema-versioned and validated; historical records retain bytes/meaning and unknown fields are rejected.
criteria.assessment: owned-records-v1 is explicitly selected and versioned; strict older modes and historical records retain their meaning.

criteria.criterion: Curator bootstrap reserves exactly one manager, activates only the real receipt identity and relinquishes canonical Task writing.
criteria.assessment: Synthetic Task reservation precedes actual manager fork; complete role/input acknowledgement and actual receipt/activation transfer the sole writer.

criteria.criterion: Existing record/configuration schemas keep their meaning; any changed grant envelope has explicit version dispatch.
criteria.assessment: Existing record/configuration/grant schemas and independent memory/ontology owner semantics remain unchanged.

criteria.criterion: Only the current confirmed manager with exact operation scope can publish Curator knowledge; ordinary workers and forged provenance fail.
criteria.assessment: Current native manager publication requires separate fresh memory and ontology grants, exact bindings and real journals/receipts/final bytes; worker/forged/stale/replay requests fail.

criteria.criterion: Activation, manager/child discovery, supervision, interrupt and resume observations are mapped without forging collaboration receipts.
criteria.assessment: Message/followup/status/wait/interruption, acknowledged release and same-ID/new-incarnation resume retain actual native and owner observations.

criteria.criterion: Effective model/effort and independent contexts are checked; missing capabilities hold work.
criteria.assessment: Astra/xhigh, full role/problem delivery, complete native pages and exact fork-prefix evidence remain; summaries and excludeTurns cannot establish context isolation.

criteria.criterion: Real observations establish identities, reservation-before-launch, one canonical writer, full required teams, settings inheritance and isolated solver input.
criteria.assessment: Compact G1 retains actual generic work, manager verification and owner publication; G2 full-team, G3 adversarial and G4 final/recovery evidence remain separate unfinished gates.

criteria.criterion: Capacity queuing preserves every required agent; uncertain or absent observations are named non-passes.
criteria.assessment: Capacity release follows acknowledged lifecycle and owner records; same-ID resume, old-epoch denial, final helper closure and all prior native IDs remain required.

criteria.criterion: Candidate writes to trusted policy/broker, canonical ledgers, control records, grants and credentials are denied by the enforced boundary.
criteria.assessment: Owned-record/header/stat observation does not replace protected-canary denial, private/canonical write confinement or final actual process evidence.

criteria.criterion: Malicious branch/diff/note/config, process execution and broker-request cases cannot gain authority or bypass publication.
criteria.assessment: Malicious-content/process/tool/network and publication-denial obligations remain mandatory; the owned-record mode grants no ambient-write or privacy exception.
